rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Actions 1.1 Shift Stones 1.2 Flip Stones 1.3 Score a Card 1.4 Ending your turn 2 Shuffling 3 End Game Condition 4 Final Scoring 5 Solo Game Variant Actions On your turn you may either skip your turn and draw 2 cards, or do as many of the following actions as you want before passing. You may not skip your turn twice in a row. When you run out of cards you'll have to end your turn. Shift Stones Discard a card, then switch any two adjacent tiles. (No diagonals.) Flip Stones Discard a card, then flip over a tile. Score a Card Reveal a card from your hand that matches a pattern on the tile grid. Place it face-up in front of you. (The card must match exactly, and may not be rotated or flipped.) Ending your turn Draw back up to 4 cards. Shuffling If the Draw pile runs out, the Discard pile will be shuffled back in. End Game Condition After any player has scored a certain number of cards, the game will end after that round is completed (all players have had an equal number of turns / start of the first player’s turn). The number of cards depends on the number of players: 2 Players, 10 Cards 3 Players, 9 Cards 4 Players, 8 Cards 5 Players, 7 Cards Final Scoring Each player's score is the total of all the points in their scored cards, plus the player with the most 1-point cards gains a bonus 3 points (in case of a 1-point card tie, each tied player gets 3 points). In case of a total-score tie, players share the victory (there is no tie breaker). Solo Game Variant Cards: 8 x 1 Point, 4 x 2 Points, 3 x 3 Points, 1 x 5 Points Goal: To win you must score all 16 Pattern cards Strike: If you end a turn without scoring at least one Pattern card you get a Strike. If you get 4 Strikes the game ends in a loss

[Rating: 1/10] Nice table presence, a card abstract game of pattern recognition. – Random card draw is a huge bear.  Draw cards that match the table state and win the game. – Small simple decision space, look at cards are any achievable this turn?  Can I set up a big point card next turn and hope my opponent doesn't turn it to custard?  – No interaction as you don't know opponents' cards.

[Rating: 1/10] Not a game. Drawing random cards is done better - and I never thought I'd utter these words - by Exploding Kittens.

[Rating: 1/10] After playing this on BGA multiple times (10) and thinking it just doesn't click, I can honestly say this game is plain bad. It is completely luck dependent, you can plan ahead but it means nothing. Your opponent can be given a hand of complete objectives without even doing anything. If you enjoy games where you can do things and not really care about the outcome I guess this would be a great one to add to your collection along with Sorry and Candyland. [Rating: 2/10] This is not really a game.  You play through your hand of cards on your turn hoping to score points.  You may get lucky. and score a lot with the cards you have.  You may score none.  What you do really doesn't influence any other players.  This could be a great pattern recognition exercise for young kids.

[Rating: 2/10] Solo play is a straight puzzle and memory game of figuring out the optimal way to cycle through your cards ensuring that you can always score one card. Some strategy to planning which ones to score early and which to save, but I don't see that as fun.  I tend not enjoy binary win/lose solo games anyway.  I might show this to my friends but I don't see the point - you don't know what scoring patters other players are going for, so any interaction is there purely to frustrate - seems like there would be 0 table talk. The color choices for opposing sides annoy me and make no intuitive sense - why

[Rating: 2/10] Shifting Stones has several issues that sully its play experience. First is the luck of the draw. It is quite possible to draw pattern cards that are already completed, or nearly completed, but also the game has a preference toward completing the easiest patterns. Since the game is triggered when a player completes a set number of patterns, and provides a bonus for completing the most 1pt patterns (which are also the easiest to complete) the game incentivizes fast and low scoring patterns.
